question: For one independently declared finite lapse toy integrand on C*, does the positive-real open ray have endpoint damping and retain the principal square-root branch under positive two-slab coordinate bookkeeping, without being promoted to a relative-homology class or gravity cycle?

upstream_results.role: pins the preceding finite endpoint/determinant-line toy and its explicitly open lapse-cycle field; it does not select the present toy ray

declared_toy.declared_open_rapid_decay_ray: Gamma_plus: N=r for r in (0,infinity), oriented from 0_plus to +infinity; no relative-homology group or class is asserted
declared_toy.branch: principal Log on C minus (-infinity,0]; principal sqrt(N)=exp(Log(N)/2)
declared_toy.endpoint_data: only the two decay ends 0_plus and +infinity of the declared ray; no Stokes coefficients or global relative-homology basis

assumptions: a and b are strictly positive real constants in this finite analytic toy
Gamma_plus is a declared open rapid-decay toy ray, not an element of a specified relative-homology group and not a derived physical initial lapse cycle
the principal branch cut is excluded by the positive two-slab domain
the coordinate map (r_1,r_2) to (T,s) is used only for positive-domain bookkeeping and has no claim of a BV-BFV quantum pushforward
no gravitational field, ghost continuum, conformal factor, endpoint polarization, or absolute measure is supplied
